descriptors.concept_name: Faceless Assessment Scheme For Escaping Income
descriptors.definition: The Central Government may notify a faceless assessment framework for processing income escaping assessment, issuing notices, or passing orders under specific tax provisions. This framework eliminates direct interfaces, optimizes resource utilization through functional specialization, and deploys team-based dynamic jurisdiction assessments.
inclusion: Assessment, reassessment or recomputation under section 147
Issuance of notice under section 148
exclusion: Regular physical proceedings not covered under the notified scheme
nearby_distinctions: Differs from conventional face-to-face scrutiny assessments by incorporating automated risk management allocations and team-based workflows.

descriptors.concept_name: Other Assessment Provisions And Transitional Rules
descriptors.definition: Escaping income assessed under specific reassessment provisions is chargeable at the tax rates applicable to the respective assessment years when the income ought to have been taxed. Additionally, assessees can claim to drop reassessment proceedings under certain conditions provided they have not contested the original order.
inclusion: Taxation of escaped income at historical rates
Assessee claims for dropping section 147 proceedings
Application of pre-amendment provisions for specified search dates
exclusion: Matters concluded by specific rectification or revision orders where appeals were challenged
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between current reassessment rules and transitional provisions applicable before specific legislative amendment dates.

descriptors.concept_name: Time Limits For Completion Of Assessments And Reassessments
descriptors.definition: Statutory time limits regulate the completion of assessments, reassessments, or fresh assessments based on the specific assessment year or the date of service of notices. These prescribed periods restrict when tax authorities must finalize orders following returns, searches, or appellate remands.
inclusion: Time limits for regular scrutiny or best judgment assessments
Time limits for reassessments following section 148 notices
Time limits for fresh orders after appellate set-aside actions
exclusion: Unspecified assessment procedures outside the statutory provisions of this section
nearby_distinctions: Varies strictly by assessment year and the specific procedural trigger such as regular filings versus appellate remands.

descriptors.definition: Income-tax authorities may amend any order, intimation, or deemed intimation to rectify mistakes that are glaring, obvious, and apparent from the record. Such rectification can encompass clear errors of fact or law, including those arising from subsequent Supreme Court interpretations or retrospective legislative amendments.
inclusion: Amendment of past assessment orders and statutory intimations
Rectification of clear legal or factual oversights without long-drawn debates
exclusion: Debatable issues requiring complex reasoning or subjective changes of opinion
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes self-evident mistakes correctable under section 154 from debatable matters requiring prolonged legal interpretations or appeals.

descriptors.definition: Assessment orders must be amended within specific time frames to reflect adjustments made in related entities or primary assessments, such as disallowances of partner remuneration or modifications in AOP/BOI incomes. These consequential amendments calculate limitation periods from the end of the financial year in which the final order for the primary entity was passed.
inclusion: Rectification of partner assessments following firm-level disallowances
Consequential adjustments to member assessments due to AOP income variations
exclusion: Standard rectifications governed strictly by general four-year limitation windows without specific cross-entity triggers
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general rectification rules by tying limitation periods directly to the final resolution date of the primary entity's assessment.

descriptors.concept_name: Notice Of Demand And Service Validation
descriptors.definition: Assessing officers must serve a notice of demand specifying any payable sum consequent to orders passed under the Act, with certain intimations automatically qualifying as notices of demand. Co-operating or appearing in assessment proceedings cures procedural defects regarding service timeliness or validity unless specifically objected to beforehand.
inclusion: Issuance of formal demand notices for taxes, penalties, or fines
Deemed demand notices arising from processing intimations
Timeline rules for paying taxes on specific perquisite shares under start-up exemptions
exclusion: Recovery proceedings undertaken without serving a valid or deemed notice of demand
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between standard notices and statutory deeming provisions where active co-operation cures minor procedural notice defects.

descriptors.concept_name: Modification And Revision Of Notice Under Insolvency Orders
descriptors.definition: When tax demands are reduced by orders from competent insolvency or appellate tribunals, the assessing officer must adjust and reissue the notice of demand in conformity with those rulings. Such modified notices operate as statutory demands under the governing tax framework.
inclusion: Demand revisions following Adjudicating Authority orders under insolvency laws
Subsequent revisions aligning demands with NCLAT or Supreme Court outcomes
exclusion: Original demands that have not undergone reduction by recognized insolvency or judicial authorities
nearby_distinctions: Applies strictly when financial liabilities are adjusted through statutory insolvency proceedings rather than normal tax appeals.

descriptors.definition: During total income assessments, the assessing officer must officially notify the assessee in writing about the computed amount of eligible carry-forward losses. This written intimation covers specific categories including business losses, speculative losses, capital losses, and racehorse maintenance losses.
inclusion: Written official orders quantifying carry-forward business and capital losses
Loss tracking for speculative businesses and racehorse activities
exclusion: Losses that are unverified or ineligible for carry-forward under statutory provisions
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general tax assessment orders by focusing exclusively on quantifying and notifying eligible carry-forward losses.

descriptors.concept_name: Faceless Rectification Amendments And Issuance Scheme
descriptors.definition: The Central Government may establish a faceless scheme for executing rectifications, statutory amendments, demand notices, and loss intimations. This framework aims to maximize operational efficiency and transparency through automated, team-based processing and dynamic jurisdiction.
inclusion: Faceless processing of rectification applications and order amendments
Team-based issuance of demand notices and loss intimations
exclusion: Manual rectification and amendment workflows not incorporated into the notification
nearby_distinctions: Applies specifically to post-assessment administrative functions like rectifications and notices rather than original scrutiny assessments.

descriptors.definition: Block assessment consolidates investigations for search and requisition cases initiated after a specific date to improve efficiency and minimize multiple proceedings. The block period spans the six preceding assessment years plus the period up to the execution of the final search authorization.
inclusion: Determination of the block period based on prior assessment years and search execution dates
Consolidated search investigations across multiple prior years
exclusion: Searches initiated outside the specified date thresholds governed by separate reassessment rules
nearby_distinctions: Replaces fragmented reassessments with a comprehensive consolidated block timeline for search-related investigations.
